answer: Forced-choice divergence attestation. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge derived from a shared sparrow beacon, and clones that share state answer identically, so the system flags any two identities returning correlated responses and requires each to diverge by committing to distinct private randomness. An attacker running N clones pays N independent ferrous hardware roots plus N separate maintenance streams, since shared infrastructure collapses under divergence testing; maintaining undetected clones thus costs full per-identity overhead, not marginal copy cost.
